evidence: Read the full argument: a,2a,...,(p-1)a reduce to a rearrangement of 1..p-1, multiply, collect a^(p-1)(p-1)!=(p-1)!, cancel via Euclid's lemma; rearrangement (nonzero, distinct) and a^p=a from the 'Simplifications' section are proved.

sourceLabel: Wikipedia, Proofs of Fermat's little theorem
evidence: Read: G={1..p-1} is a group (inverses via Bezout), order k of a gives subgroup, Lagrange gives k | p-1, so a^(p-1)=1; a=0 and the a^p form are covered in 'Simplifications'.

Read: p=2 trivial; for odd p each nonzero residue has a unique inverse, a=a^-1 only for a=+-1 (Euclid's lemma on a^2-1), the rest pair off with product 1, giving (p-1)!=-1; worked p=11 example. Phrased via field/inverses rather than the word 'group', but the same argument.
Read: termination from |r_i|<|r_(i-1)|; gcd(x,0)=x and gcd(x,y)=gcd(y,x-zy) proved by common divisors, so the last nonzero remainder is gcd(a,b).

preciseLocator: Section "Bezout's identity" (together with 'Proof of validity' for gcd = last nonzero remainder)
evidence: Read: g=r_(N-1)=r_(N-3)-q_(N-1) r_(N-2), then successively substitute r_k=r_(k-2)-q_k r_(k-1) back to r_0=a-q_0 b, giving g=sa+tb. Last nonzero remainder = gcd is proved in 'Proof of validity'.

Read: least positive element d of {ax+by} is shown by Euclidean division to divide a and b, and any common divisor divides d, so d=gcd. This is the subgroup/least-element argument, but the lattice-point/projection framing and 'every subgroup of Z is dZ' are not stated.
sketchProblem: Sketch looks wrong: vectors (a,b) in Z^2 project to aZ, not aZ+bZ; should be the image of Z^2 under (x,y)->ax+by.

preciseLocator: Density of the rationals, part ii) (case 0<=x<y, then sign cases)
evidence: Read: Archimedean property gives n with n(y-x)>1, then m = least integer > nx (= floor(nx)+1 by well-ordering), so nx<m<=nx+1<ny, hence x<m/n<y. Floor is expressed as least element, same construction.
